notes:
Setup opens straight away, and only one of it. A click used to produce
nothing for up to fifteen seconds while the installer unpacked itself, so
people clicked again - and again - until twenty copies were running. It now
shows a splash immediately, reaches its own window in about a second and a
half, and a second copy brings the first one to the front instead of starting
another.

Room music plays. The queue was in step on the server while the window
refused to start audio nothing had clicked on, so nobody heard anything.

Achievements without a Steam API key. Nyxen reads your achievements from your
own Steam profile page, so there is no key to create and nothing to paste - it
offers the accounts Steam has already signed in on your PC and you pick one. A
key stays optional and buys only two things: games you own but have not
installed, and reading a profile that is not public.

Updates inside the app. It checks for a new version, tells you what changed,
and installs it with one button. The download is checked against its published
SHA-256 before anything is run.

Setup can repair or remove. Running the installer when Nyxen is already
installed now offers Repair and Uninstall instead of silently reinstalling, and
the window itself has been rebuilt.

Rooms work. Opening a room used to load it into a hidden pane, which made Join
voice and the room's shared modpacks unreachable. Voice also shows who is
talking, with an icon when somebody is muted or not listening, and the DJ has
to be in the call to play music.

Choose your microphone and your headphones - in Settings, and in the call
itself, where you notice you picked the wrong one. Changing either takes effect
immediately without dropping the call.

Invite links can be pasted at any time. There is now one "Use an invite link"
box, reachable from Social and from Settings as well as the sign-in screen, so
a link that arrives after you already have an account is not a dead end - and
you can switch back to your own server just as easily.

Letting a friend in is one button. Nyxen opens the tunnel itself - no terminal
window, no port forwarding, no router settings - and the invite carries the
address, so the person you send it to does not have to type anything either.
